question.problem: By the multiplicative property of congruences, ${12}^{6}≡$
question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we decompose the exponent into a product of smaller exponents. For example,

$$
{12}^{6}=(3\cdot 4)^{6}={3}^{3}\cdot {3}^{3}\cdot {4}^{3}\cdot {4}^{3}.
$$

Next, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{3} & ≡27\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡3\cdot 9+0\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡3\cdot 0+0\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡0\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {4}^{3} & ≡64\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡7\cdot 9+1\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡7\cdot 0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{12}^{6} & ≡{3}^{3}\cdot {3}^{3}\cdot {4}^{3}\cdot {4}^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡0\cdot 0\cdot 1\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡0\, & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{12}^{6}≡0\,\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$
